category_title: Boys who project personal experiences of physical abuse onto bullying behavior
minimal_context: The student and researcher are participating in an individual 20-minute role-play activity using semi-structured scripts to discuss a bullying incident.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are going to do a 20-minute role-play activity using this script and scarf. Let's look at the second part of the script. Who do you think the victim could talk to about the bullying incident?

STUDENT: He could talk only with his grandparents and his teacher.

TUTOR: What about the bully? What could be a solution for him?

STUDENT: Apology would be the right thing to do in order to ﬁnd a way out of his problem but at the same time it would be a mistake since by apologising he would show weakness and nobody would hold him in high esteem anymore.

TUTOR: Let's think about the bully's intentions. Why do you think the bully acted aggressively during the incident?

STUDENT: Maybe his father had hit him that morning and he was so sad …he didn ’t really want to harm the other child.

options.A: Augment tactics during the role-play, such as response promotion and disruption, and reallocate responding to script options associated with contingent reinforcement during the session.
options.B: Meet the student individually, inform them about the focus of the role-play project on difficult behavior, assure them that their data will be confidential, and give them the option not to participate.
options.C: Radically remove time constraints for the role-play activity, slowing down the pace of the semi-structured scripts as much as required by the individual student.
options.D: Use a visual schedule that identifies the role-play activities of the day and the reinforcers the student is eligible to receive during the individual meeting.
